newsitem.title: UK: BP to sue Greenpeace over oil protest.
newsitem.headline: BP to sue Greenpeace over oil protest.

text.p: British Petroleum Co. Plc is suing Greenpeace for 1.4 million pounds ($2.3 million) after four protesters belonging to the group occupied a BP oil rig in the North Atlantic, the environmental group said Monday.
Greenpeace said BP had issued the claim in Scotland's highest civil court, the Court of Session, against the environmental group and the four activists who took part in the protest.

BP confirmed it was taking legal action against the environmental campaign group to try to reclaim more than 1 million pounds ($620 million). It said this represented the cost of the halting of the platform's progress to its destination in the Foinaven field.
"Their actions were unlawful and we are now seeking redress," a BP spokesman told Reuters.
Greenpeace said a hearing where BP will call for an interim ruling against the group was due to be held Tuesday.
The Greenpeace activists clambered aboard the Stena Dee floating platform, which was heading from Norway to the Foinaven field some 100 miles off the coast of Scotland, just over a week ago.
The protest was aimed at halting oil exploration in the area, but Greenpeace called off the occupation Sunday, saying it could no longer guarantee the safety of the protesters.
The four were each fined 200 pounds ($124) in a Scottish court Monday for their part in the action.
Greenpeace had also been blocking an Alantic Richfield Co. rig off the Alaskan coast to keep it away from a field in the arctic Beaufort Sea.
A U.S. judge ordered the activists Friday to stay outside a moving safety buffer around the mobile rig.
The blockades, aimed at fighting global warming, are part of Greenpeace's most ambitious campaign yet against the oil industry.
The group wants oil producers to switch to renewable resources, arguing that burning even existing reserves of fossil fuels will cause irreversible climate change.
